fields.current: Should recall ballots drop the replacement question, with vacancies filled by succession, special election or appointment instead?

evidence.location: A YES vote on this measure means
evidence.excerpt: Recall elections would no longer include a question about who should fill the vacancy. Instead, vacancies typically would be filled through special elections or appointments, depending on the office and timing.

fields.explanation: Restates the YES meaning.

fields.current: Recall ballots for state officers ask only whether to remove the official. If a governor is recalled, the Lieutenant Governor becomes governor, but a recall in the first two years of the term, before the next statewide nomination period closes, triggers a special election to pick a governor for the rest of the term. Other recalled offices are filled under existing rules, usually a special election for legislators and a governor's appointment for other statewide offices.

evidence.excerpt: If the Governor is recalled before the close of the nomination period for the next statewide election during the first two years of the term, the Lieutenant Governor serves as Governor until voters elect a new Governor at a future statewide election.
If the Governor is recalled later in the term, the Lieutenant Governor serves as Governor for the rest of the term.
a special election shall be called to replace the Governor and shall be consolidated with the statewide primary election.
the top two vote-getters shall compete in a special election consolidated with the subsequent statewide general election
during the first two years of the Governor's term, a special election shall be called to replace the Governor, be consolidated with the statewide primary election
Except for the office of the Governor, Proposition 5 uses the existing process for filling vacancies to fill the office.
a replacement typically would be elected through a separate special election.
The Governor would choose who would fill a vacancy in any other office (other than office of the Governor).

fields.explanation: Most of it is supported. The legal text calls a special election consolidated with the next statewide primary, with a top-two runoff at the general election if no one wins a majority. 'Triggers a special election' reads as an immediate election. LAO describes it as the Lieutenant Governor serving until voters elect a new Governor at a future statewide election.
fields.proposedText: Recall ballots for state officers ask only whether to remove the official. If a governor is recalled, the Lieutenant Governor becomes governor. If the recall happens in the first two years of the term, before the next statewide nomination period closes, a special election held with the next statewide primary picks a governor for the rest of the term. Other recalled offices are filled under existing rules, usually a special election for legislators and a governor's appointment for other statewide offices.
fields.limitations: Legal text read through GrowSF's reproduction (independent) and the Senate Elections Committee analysis of the January 30, 2023 version. The SOS legal text PDF was not fetched.

fields.current: Supporters' official argument says replacements should be chosen in regular elections, not by a small plurality on a recall ballot.

evidence.excerpt: Proposition 5 preserves your power to recall an official by majority vote while closing the loophole that allows a replacement candidate to take office with a small fraction of the vote.
It should never be used as a tactic to 'redo' an election as a political or partisan scheme.

fields.explanation: The argument says a replacement should not take office with a small fraction of the vote and recalls should not redo an election. It does not say replacements should be chosen in regular elections.
fields.proposedText: Supporters' official argument says a replacement should not take office with a small fraction of the vote, and recalls should not be used to redo an election.

fields.current: Opponents' official argument says it takes away voters' power to pick a replacement and hands the choice to Sacramento insiders.

evidence.excerpt: Proposition 5 will take away your voice and erode your ability to remove and replace failed or corrupt politicians from office.
Instead, Sacramento political insiders would decide what happens next.

fields.explanation: The official argument says this.

conflicts: LAO says the Lieutenant Governor serves 'until voters elect a new Governor at a future statewide election'. The reproduced legal text and Senate analysis call it a 'special election' consolidated with the statewide primary. Same event described two ways.

AG summary says the Lieutenant Governor becomes Governor 'for the remainder of the term or until a successor is elected'. Legal text as reproduced says 'for the remainder of the unexpired term', with the special-election exception.
